steps: Lithium behaves differently from the other alkali metals because its atom and ion are very small.
Its small size gives the lithium ion a high charge density and strong polarising power.
Lithium is harder and has higher melting and boiling points than the other alkali metals; it is also the least reactive.
When heated in oxygen, lithium forms the normal oxide, Li₂O, whereas the heavier alkali metals form peroxides or superoxides.
Lithium reacts directly with nitrogen to form lithium nitride, Li₃N.
items.finalAnswer: Lithium’s small size and high charge density cause its anomalous behaviour: it is harder and less reactive, has higher melting and boiling points, and forms Li₂O and Li₃N.
